rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.fn` is the prescribed signature. The requirement declares `pub async fn search_text(&self, query: &TextQuery) -> Result<TextMatches, SourceError>` in `impl Sources`. A version that returned the same results through a different signature would not meet the text. Examples would be a synchronous function, one taking `TextQuery` by value, or one with a different error type. The signature is therefore a real structural obligation. The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs#impl[Sources]/fn[search_text]` meets it exactly. It is a `pub async fn` in `impl Sources`, takes `&self` and `query: &TextQuery`, and returns `Result<TextMatches, SourceError>`. It carries the `{impl}` marker for the requirement. The body only delegates to `self.analysis.provider.search_text(query).await`. The text names no delegation target, so the choice of provider is discretionary and needs no further root. No other items need references.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.fn` only declares the signature of `Sources::search_text`. It is an async method that takes `&TextQuery` and returns `Result<TextMatches, SourceError>`. The text has no MUST, MUST NOT or SHOULD clause about runtime behavior, so the signature is a structural obligation. Search semantics such as scope, ignore rules and completeness belong to `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.behavior` and `requirements.sdk.graph.search.source_scope`. Those are assessed separately. The test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` calls `sources.search_text(&TextQuery::new(..))`, awaits it and unwraps or inspects the `Result`. That exercises the signature, and the test is already marked as a test of this requirement. No behavioral obligation here needs more test evidence.
